guitar.modelsText: Gibson Les Paul Standard / Fender Telecaster / Danelectro
guitar.evidence: Jimmy Page's 1959 Gibson Les Paul ('Number One') is one of the most iconic guitars in rock history, alongside his well-documented use of a Telecaster (Stairway to Heaven solo) and Danelectro for alternate tunings.

blocks.purpose: Clean up ambient noise and hum.
Add gentle sustain and smooth out strumming dynamics.
blocks.gap: The Comp module is used to emulate the natural attack of acoustic picking, compensating for the lack of a dedicated clean boost/compressor.

blocks.purpose: Keep the signal path clean and transparent.
Provide a clean, natural American tone suitable for folk music.
blocks.gap: The US Deluxe is the best choice for a non-aggressive, clear sound required by the acoustic genre.

blocks.purpose: Emulate a small, natural sounding speaker cabinet.
blocks.gap: The US 2x12 provides the necessary size and clarity for an intimate acoustic setting.

blocks.purpose: Bypass the wah pedal to maintain a natural tone.
Slight tonal shaping to enhance the natural acoustic character.
blocks.gap: Used for subtle EQ adjustments, as no specific tone-shaping module is required beyond the amp/cab.

blocks.purpose: Add subtle depth and space without sounding artificial.
blocks.gap: A very minimal delay is used to enhance the 'room' feel, keeping it from distracting the strumming pattern.

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism for a more authentic acoustic folk setting.
